summary: Backend-only verification of the new recipients_sample + action_url diagnostic capture on the /api/debug/last-push-events HTML page, plus the trigger-alert filter behavior. All 9 new tests in test_recipients_sample_diagnostic.py pass, and the full backend suite is 75/75 green (no regressions). Verified: (a) diag-A and diag-B register and appear in /api/debug/devices; (b) GET /api/debug/test-push?token=Pt3481pt renders an event card whose <code> recipients_sample contains diag-A AND diag-B, action_url row shows '/', and 'recipients in chunk' + 'first recipients:' labels are present; (c) POST /api/trigger-alert with {triggeredBy:'dashboard'} (no rogue device yet) renders a card with title 'EARTHQUAKE ALERT', action_url '/alert', and recipients_sample containing diag-A AND diag-B (filter changes nothing when no matching row); (d) After registering a rogue device with user_id='dashboard', trigger-alert recipients_sample NO LONGER contains 'dashboard' but still contains diag-A/diag-B — proving the {'$ne': triggeredBy} filter works; test-push recipients_sample STILL contains 'dashboard' because test-push uses no filter. Regressions: legacy /api/status GET+POST, /api/debug/devices, POST /api/trigger-alert 200 JSON contract, send_push HTTPException(500) contract on upstream 401, and the 20-entry ring buffer bound all still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py send_push captures event['recipients_sample']=chunk[:5] and event['action_url']=data.get('action_url') as specified (lines 148, 151). debug_last_push_events HTML renders 'action_url:' and 'first recipients:' rows only for kind!='register' events (lines 372-375) — correct: register events show user_id/platform instead. HTML escaping via _html.escape is applied to every user-controlled value going into the DOM.

Note (already known): send_push chunk_size=100, so recipients_sample=chunk[:5] only shows the first 5 of the FIRST chunk of each POST. If the device count exceeds 100 there will be multiple event cards per trigger, each with its own recipients_sample of the corresponding chunk. That is intentional and matches spec.

server.py is 455 lines — well under the 700-line threshold; no refactor needed. No hardcoded URLs; all env-driven. MongoDB _id is excluded via projection in every find(). testID checks N/A (backend-only).
seed_data_creation: Test fixture snapshots the entire push_devices collection into memory, wipes it (so recipients_sample=chunk[:5] is deterministic and diag-A/diag-B are guaranteed to appear), registers 'diag-A' (tokA) and 'diag-B' (tokB), and later 'dashboard' (ROGUE) for the filter test. All three are deleted and the original collection contents restored in fixture teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The event ring buffer is process-local (deque maxlen=20) so restarting the backend clears it — several test modules rely on _restart_backend_and_wait() for isolation. When adding new diagnostic-visibility tests, remember that recipients_sample is chunk[:5] where chunk is Mongo's find() insertion order; wipe push_devices if you need deterministic ordering (see _snapshot_and_wipe_all_devices / _restore_devices in test_recipients_sample_diagnostic.py).
